scope: Curriculum and exercise-code review; no learner proficiency assessment

path.sub: Hello, thank you, small talk, and set phrases to get by
Coffee, tea and bread, and ordering at a café or a restaurant
Who does what: I am, I speak, questions and "not"
Counting, prices, days, times and your daily routine
To, in and from: places change their endings
Describing words, my and your, and "to me it pleases"
Can, must and want + a verb, and "I will"
"I was", "I went", and joining sentences with and, but, because
Hotels, trains, the body, and when something goes wrong
Opinions, reactions, and keeping a chat going
Animals, Lithuanian culture, and the sounds of the letters

units.title: Pradžia
units.tip: Lithuanian has no words for "a" or "the". Labas on its own is for friends; Sveiki is for strangers, groups and anyone older. Labas rytas, Laba diena and Labas vakaras (good morning, day, evening) are fine with anyone.

lessons.title: I am, you are, we are
Names, where you're from, coffee or tea

units.title: Pokalbis
units.tip: Most conversations start the same way. Someone asks Kaip sekasi? (How are you?), you answer, and you bounce it back with O tau? (And you?). Nobody expects more than that from a beginner.

items.en: How do you say that in Lithuanian?
Can you repeat that? (to a friend)

units.title: Maistas
units.tip: After noriu (I want) the thing you want changes ending: kava becomes kavos, arbata becomes arbatos. You will see this "some of" ending everywhere.

units.title: Restorane
units.tip: Aš norėčiau (I would like) is the polite way to order; Aš noriu (I want) is blunter. Tap water is safe but you have to ask for it; waiters will bring bottled by default.

units.title: Kalbėti
units.tip: Verbs change their ending to show who is doing it: aš kalbu (I speak), tu kalbi (you speak). Because the ending already says who, people often drop aš and tu. Put ne on the front to say "not": nesuprantu, I don't understand.

items.en: Do you speak English? (to a friend)

units.title: Veiksmai
units.tip: Every verb works like kalbu / kalbi / kalba: -u for I, -i for you, and the plain stem for he, she and they. For "we" add -me, for polite or plural "you" add -te: kalbame, kalbate.

items.en: What are you doing? (to a friend)

units.title: Maži žodžiai
units.tip: Little words do the most work. Ir (and), bet (but), nes (because) and todėl (so) join two ideas; jau (already), dar (still, yet) and tik (only) change what a sentence means. Kai (when), jeigu (if), kad (that) and nors (though) start a second idea. From here on, the conversations use them.

units.title: Dažni žodžiai
units.tip: These are among the words Lithuanians say most. Jį and ją are "him" and "her" as the thing you see or love; jam, jai, mums and jums are "to him", "to her", "to us" and "to you". Learn them inside the phrases and they come naturally.

units.title: Klausimai
units.tip: Question words go first, just like English. Learn these six and you can ask about anything by pointing. Add Ar to the front of a sentence to turn it into a yes/no question.

units.title: Apie mane
units.tip: Iš means "from", and the place after it changes its ending: iš Lietuvos (from Lithuania), iš Amerikos (from America). Jobs change for women too: mokytojas is a male teacher, mokytoja a female one.

items.en: What do you do for work?

units.title: Skaičiai
units.tip: Numbers 1 to 9 change their ending to match a "him" or a "her" word. The forms here are the masculine ones you count with.

units.title: Laikas
units.tip: Days are numbered: pirmadienis is "first day" (Monday), antradienis "second day", and so on up to sekmadienis, Sunday. Months are named after nature: July is named after the linden tree.

units.title: Mano diena
units.tip: Daily routines are full of verbs ending in -uosi or -iuosi (keliuosi, prausiuosi). That ending means you do it to yourself: I get myself up, I wash myself.

items.en: Every day I go for a walk

units.title: Galiu, turiu, reikia
units.tip: Galiu (I can), turiu (I have to) and noriu (I want) are all followed by a verb ending in -ti: galiu padėti. "I need" is said "to me it is needed": man reikia.

items.en: Can you help me? (to a friend)

lessons.title: I need, I have to · part 1
I need, I have to · part 2

units.title: Mieste
units.tip: Kur yra ...? works for any place. Answers come as directions: kairėn, dešinėn, tiesiai. "Čia" is here and "ten" is there.

units.title: Susikalbėti
units.tip: Short phrases that smooth every interaction. The -ite endings (atleiskite, parodykite) are the polite forms you use with strangers.

items.en: How do I get to the centre?

units.title: Transportas
units.tip: Lithuanian buses and trains are cheap and on time. The place you are going to takes į plus a changed ending: Kaunas becomes į Kauną, centras (the centre) becomes į centrą.

items.text: Ar šis autobusas važiuoja į centrą?
items.en: Does this bus go to the centre?
Where are you going? (by car or bus)

units.title: Parduotuvėje
units.tip: Prices are in euros. Kiek kainuoja? works for anything you can point at. Most shops take cards, but markets (turgus) are cash.

units.title: Drabužiai
units.tip: Lots of clothes are always plural in Lithuanian, even when there is only one: marškiniai (a shirt), kelnės (trousers), džinsai (jeans). Describing words then go plural too.

units.title: Spalvos
units.tip: Adjectives agree with the noun: žalias obuolys (a green apple, a "him" word) but balta duona (white bread, a "her" word). Swap -as for -a.

units.title: Aprašymai
units.tip: Describing words follow the "him / her" rule: -as, -is or -us for a "him" word, -a, -i for a "her" word. Mano brolis aukštas, mano sesuo aukšta. "Is" is usually left out.

units.title: Šeima
units.tip: Masculine nouns usually end in -as, -is or -us; feminine ones in -a or -ė. Draugas is a male friend, draugė a female friend.

units.title: Apie šeimą
units.tip: After neturiu (I don't have) the noun takes its "of" ending: neturiu brolio. In questions with Ar turi...? one thing takes the same ending as after noriu (ar turi brolį?), and things you count take the "of" form (ar turi brolių?). Don't try to master it. Say it slightly wrong and people still understand you.

items.en: Do you have brothers or sisters?

units.title: Darbai
units.tip: Jobs have a "him" and a "her" form, like mokytojas / mokytoja (teacher). "In" a workplace is just an ending: ligoninė → ligoninėje, mokykla → mokykloje.

units.title: Oras ir jausmai
units.tip: Feelings often use "man" (to me): Man šalta is "I'm cold", literally "to me it is cold". Man patinka is "I like it", literally "to me it pleases".

units.title: Namai
units.tip: Namai (home) and durys (door) are always plural. "In" a room is an ending: kambarys → kambaryje. Commands to a friend end in -k: atidaryk, uždaryk.

units.title: Veiksmažodžiai
units.tip: Dictionary forms end in -ti. For "I", the ending becomes -u (kalbu, noriu); for "you", -i (kalbi, nori). You have been using these all along.

units.title: Laisvalaikis
units.tip: Man patinka (I like it) is built backwards: literally "to me it pleases". To say what you like doing, use Aš mėgstu plus a verb ending in -ti: Aš mėgstu skaityti, I like to read.

items.en: What do you like to do?
What are you doing at the weekend?

units.title: Planai
units.tip: For times, use the "at" form of the number: septintą valandą means "at seven o'clock". Gal (maybe) is the friendliest way to suggest anything: Gal rytoj? Maybe tomorrow?

items.en: Do you want to go together?

units.title: Metų laikai
units.tip: Seasons and months are named after nature: liepa (July) is the linden tree, birželis (June) the birch. Learn them with the weather they bring.

units.title: Ateitis
units.tip: The future is easy: add -siu for "I will": dirbti → dirbsiu, valgyti → valgysiu. For "you will" it is -si. "It will be" is simply bus.

items.en: In the evening I will be at home
Where will you go on holiday?
In summer I'll go to the seaside
I will be in Lithuania for a week
We will stay in a hotel

units.title: Jungtukai
units.tip: Joining words turn short phrases into real sentences. A comma goes before bet (but), nes (because), todėl (so) and kad (that). In questions, "or" is ar: arbatos ar kavos?

items.en: I'm not going because it's raining
It's raining, so I'm staying home

units.title: Vakar
units.tip: For "I did", most verbs end in -au or -iau: dirbau (I worked), valgiau (I ate), mačiau (I saw). "I was" is buvau, and "it was" is buvo.

units.title: Ką veikei?
units.tip: Asking about the past, "you" ends in -ai or -ei: kur buvai? ką veikei? For he, she and they it ends in -o: jis buvo. "We" is -ome / -ėme: buvome, valgėme.

items.en: In the morning I went to the park

units.title: Kelionė
units.tip: Lithuania's three big cities are Vilnius (capital), Kaunas and Klaipėda on the coast. The Curonian Spit, a long sand dune in the Baltic, is the country's most famous landscape.

units.title: Viešbutyje
units.tip: Hotel staff almost always speak English, but opening in Lithuanian gets a warmer welcome. Vienai nakčiai (for one night) and dviem naktims (for two nights) cover most stays.

units.title: Kūnas ir sveikata
units.tip: To say what hurts, use man skauda plus the body part with an -ą, -į or -ę ending: koja → koją, dantis → dantį. A cold is sloga, said "to me": man sloga.

items.text: Ar turite vaistų nuo galvos skausmo?
items.en: Do you have something for a headache?

units.title: Pagalba
units.tip: The emergency number is 112 and operators speak English. Pharmacies (vaistinė) are everywhere and pharmacists can advise on minor things without a doctor.

units.title: Nuomonė
units.tip: Opinions start with Aš manau, kad... (I think that...) or Man atrodo, kad... (it seems to me that...). To compare, use geresnė už (better than) and man labiau patinka (I prefer).

units.title: Pokalbio įgūdžiai
units.tip: Little words keep a conversation alive: beje (by the way), na (well...), rimtai? (seriously?). When you run out of words, ask a question back: o tu?, papasakok daugiau.

items.en: How long have you been here?

units.title: Gyvūnai
units.tip: The stork (gandras) is Lithuania's national bird. Seeing the first one in spring is said to bring a good year.

units.title: Kultūra
units.tip: Lithuanian is one of the oldest living Indo-European languages and the closest to Sanskrit still spoken. Some of these words have no English equivalent at all.

units.title: Garsai
units.tip: Lithuanian spelling is very regular: each letter keeps its sound, and every letter is said. What isn't written is which part of a word is strong, and its pitch, so listen for those. Most letters sound like English. These are the ones that trick people: c = "ts", j = "y", š = "sh", ž = the "s" in "measure", č = "ch". The words here are ones English has too (pizza, giraffe), so you can hear the letters in words you can guess.

lessons.title: Long vowels, ie and the rolled r

conversations.title: Labas vakaras!
conversations.scene: Evening, on the stairs of your new building in Vilnius. Your neighbour Danutė is coming home with a bag of shopping.

conversations.title: Labas, Rūta!
conversations.scene: You are Tomas, on your first day in Vilnius. It's late morning, the café is busy, and the only free seat is next to a woman with a coffee.

lines.en: Please. (She points at the free seat.)

lines.text: Aš esu Rūta. Koks tavo vardas?

conversations.title: Dar kartą, prašau
conversations.scene: The next day you meet Rūta again, on a bench by the river. She talks fast and uses a few words you haven't learned yet. That's the point: you know how to slow her down and ask.

lines.en: Shall we go for a walk? (She says it very fast.)
Shall we... go for a walk?
To go for a walk... look! (She walks two fingers along the bench.)
How do you say that in Lithuanian?

conversations.title: Kalbų vakaras
conversations.scene: Rūta takes you to a language evening at a café, where people swap languages over tea. A woman called Laura sits down next to you.

lines.text: Labas! Aš esu Laura. Tu esi Tomas?
lines.en: Hi! I'm Laura. Are you Tomas?
Nice to meet you! Do you speak Lithuanian?

lines.text: Labai gerai! O aš mokausi anglų kalbos.
lines.en: Very good! And I'm learning English.

lines.text: Ar nori arbatos, ar kavos, ar vandens, ar...
lines.en: Would you like tea, or coffee, or water, or... (She says it all very fast.)
Here you go. And what are you reading?

lines.text: Puiku! O Rūta? Ar ji čia?
lines.en: Great! And Rūta? Is she here?

conversations.title: Kur tu?
conversations.scene: You are meeting Rūta and Jonas at the station for a day trip, but you are running late. Rūta texts you.

lines.text: Mes laukiame stotyje. Ar tu ateini?
lines.en: We're waiting at the station. Are you coming?
Yes, I'm coming! I'm in a hurry.

lines.text: Ar tu matai? Mes čia, stotyje!
lines.en: Can you see it? We're here, at the station!
Do you hear that? (The train is coming in!)
Yes, I hear it! Wait for me!

conversations.title: Atsiprašau!
conversations.scene: You are meeting Rūta at a café in the old town, but you have lost your way. A man called Antanas is walking his dog nearby.

lines.en: That's Reksas! (Her dog wags his tail.)
The senamiestis... here, look! (She points at the old houses: the old town.) Do you speak English?
A little. Do you speak English?

lines.text: Restoranas? Tiesiai, tiesiai, paskui dešinėn, ir...
lines.en: The restaurant? Straight, straight, then right, and... (She says it very fast.)
Got it! Thank you very much!

lines.text: Nieko! O kodėl jūs čia, Vilniuje?
lines.en: Not at all! And why are you here, in Vilnius?
I live in Lithuania and I'm learning.

conversations.title: Meet Jonas
conversations.scene: Rūta brings you to a party and introduces her friend Jonas.

lines.en: Nice to meet you. Where are you from?

lines.text: Aš esu iš Amerikos. O tu?
lines.en: I am from America. What about you?

lines.text: Aš esu iš Kauno. Kur tu gyveni?
lines.en: I'm from Kaunas. Where do you live?
I live in Vilnius. What about you?
I live in Vilnius too, in the old town.
What do you do for work?

lines.text: Taip, mano darbas įdomus! O kuo tu dirbi?
lines.en: Yes, my job is interesting! And what do you do?

conversations.title: Sekmadienio pietūs
conversations.scene: Rūta takes you to her parents' house in the countryside for Sunday lunch. Her dad, Vytautas, is cooking.

lines.en: Good day! Nice to meet you.
Nice to meet you! Are you hungry?
Here you go, here is the coffee.
And a beer? It's very good!

lines.text: Štai sriuba, duona ir sūris. Skanaus!
lines.en: Here is soup, bread and cheese. Enjoy your meal!
Here you go, here is the salt.
Thank you, Tomas! It was very nice.

conversations.title: Restorane
conversations.scene: Jonas takes you to lunch at a restaurant in the old town. The waitress, Eglė, meets you at the door.

lines.en: Good afternoon! A table for two, please.
This way, please. Here is the menu. Some water?

lines.text: O aš norėčiau kavos su pienu.
lines.en: And I would like coffee with milk.
Cepelinai (big potato dumplings) with meat. Very tasty!
Here you go. (She brings the bill.)

conversations.title: Asking the way
conversations.scene: You need the train station. You stop a man on the street.

lines.text: Žinoma. Mes esame čia, o stotis yra ten.
lines.en: Of course. We are here, and the station is there.
Got it! Thank you very much!

conversations.title: Į Kauną
conversations.scene: You are going to Kaunas for the day. First the ticket window at the Vilnius bus station, then a taxi in Kaunas.

lines.en: Good afternoon! Where are you going?

lines.text: Laba diena! Bilietą į Kauną, prašau.
lines.en: Good afternoon! A ticket to Kaunas, please.
Thanks! And when does it arrive?
Yes. Take me to the hotel.

conversations.title: Pamestas lagaminas
conversations.scene: You flew home from a trip, but your suitcase didn't. You go to the lost luggage desk at Vilnius airport.

lines.en: Good afternoon! How can I help?
Good afternoon! Where is my suitcase?
OK, let's have a look. What is your suitcase like?

lines.text: Ne, jis mėlynas. Mano lagaminas juodas.
lines.en: No, it's blue. My suitcase is black.

lines.text: Atsiprašau! O šitas? Didelis, juodas ir labai sunkus!
lines.en: Sorry! And this one? Big, black and very heavy!
All good. Here you are, your suitcase.

conversations.title: Šeimos nuotraukos
conversations.scene: Over coffee, Jonas shows you photos of his family on his phone.

lines.text: Jis labai linksmas ir protingas. Ir aukštas!
lines.en: He is very cheerful and clever. And tall!

lines.text: O tu? Ar turi brolių ar seserų?
lines.en: And you? Do you have brothers or sisters?

lines.text: O čia mano mama ir tėtis.
lines.en: And here are my mom and dad.

conversations.title: Traukinyje
conversations.scene: On the train home from Kaunas, a woman sits down next to you. She looks very tired.

lines.en: Excuse me, is this seat free?

lines.text: Aš dirbu ligoninėje. Aš esu slaugytoja.
lines.en: I work in a hospital. I am a nurse.
Yes, but my job is hard.
And you? What do you do for work?
I work twelve hours a day!
My stop! It was very nice!

conversations.title: Jauskis kaip namie
conversations.scene: It's a cold, rainy evening. Laura, from the language evening, has invited you to see her new flat.

lines.text: Labas! Užeik, užeik! Koks šiandien oras?
lines.en: Hi! Come in, come in! What's the weather like today?
Make yourself at home. Sit down!
Thanks! Your flat is very beautiful.

lines.text: Ačiū! Bet jis mažas. Čia svetainė, ten virtuvė, o ten miegamasis.
lines.en: Thanks! But it's small. Here is the living room, there the kitchen, and there the bedroom.
Here is the tea. It's hot!
It's cold in the room, isn't it?

conversations.title: Prie ežero?
conversations.scene: Saturday morning. It's raining, and Jonas texts you about going to the lake.

lines.en: Hi! Are we going to the lake today?
I'm not going, because it's raining.

lines.text: Lyja tik ryte. Po pietų bus saulė!
lines.en: It's only raining in the morning. In the afternoon there'll be sun!
OK, but I haven't eaten yet.

lines.text: Puiku! Mano sesuo irgi nori. Gerai?
lines.en: Great! My sister wants to come too. OK?
Great! Two o'clock by the station.

conversations.title: Aš pavėlavau
conversations.scene: You were meant to meet Rūta at a restaurant at ten. It's eleven.

lines.en: Hi! I've been waiting an hour already!

lines.text: Ne, ne! Aš nežinojau, kur yra restoranas.
lines.en: No, no! I didn't know where the restaurant was.
I didn't know where the restaurant was.
OK, never mind. And this morning?
Aha! That's why you were late!

lines.text: Ir kitą kartą – ne taip vėlai!
lines.en: And next time, not so late!

conversations.title: Klaipėdoje
conversations.scene: You get off the train in Klaipėda, on the coast. You want to see the sea, so you ask a woman at the station.

lines.en: Excuse me! Where is the sea?
The sea? It's far. Take a bus.

lines.text: Ačiū! O kur yra autobusų stotis?
lines.en: Thanks! And where is the bus station?

lines.text: Ten, tiesiai, paskui dešinėn. Jūs turistas?
lines.en: Over there, straight on, then right. Are you a tourist?

lines.text: Sveiki atvykę! Ar jau matėte jūrą?
lines.en: Welcome to Klaipėda! Have you seen the sea yet?
I like the forest and the sea!

lines.text: Bet jūsų lagaminas didelis. Gal taksi?
lines.en: But your suitcase is big. Maybe a taxi?
OK, the bus then! Good luck!
The taxis are over there, by the station.

conversations.title: Pas gydytoją
conversations.scene: Too long on a windy beach: you have caught a cold. The hotel sends you to a doctor, Daiva.

lines.en: Good afternoon. I caught a cold.

lines.text: Taip, aš kosėju. Ir man sloga.
lines.en: Yes, I'm coughing. And I have a runny nose.
I see. That's from the coughing.
Can I go to the sea?
No! Bed and tea, for three days.

conversations.title: Policijoje
conversations.scene: Back in Vilnius, your bag is stolen in the old town. You go to the police station.

lines.text: Ar jums viskas gerai? Ar reikia gydytojo?
lines.en: Are you all right? Do you need a doctor?
OK. For the passport, go to the embassy.

conversations.title: Vėl kalbų vakare
conversations.scene: Months later, you go back to the language evening. This time you speak only Lithuanian. A man called Paulius sits down next to you.

lines.text: Labas! Aš Paulius. Tu irgi mokaisi lietuvių kalbos?
lines.en: Hi! I'm Paulius. Are you learning Lithuanian too?

lines.text: Aš esu iš Amerikos. O tu?
lines.en: I am from America. And you?

lines.text: Aš esu iš Kauno, bet gyvenu Vilniuje.
lines.en: I'm from Kaunas, but I live in Vilnius.
How long have you been here?

lines.text: Labai! Aš dirbu muziejuje. Rytoj ten ekskursija lietuviškai!
lines.en: Very much! I work at a museum. Tomorrow there's a tour there in Lithuanian!
At five o'clock. Will you come?

lines.text: Aštuoni, šeši, penki... Štai. Parašyk man!
lines.en: Eight, six, five... There. Text me!
It was nice to talk. See you tomorrow!

conversations.title: At the market
conversations.scene: Saturday at the market (turgus). You want some apples.

lines.en: Good day! What would you like?
Good day! Do you have apples?
Yes, of course! Red or green?
Here you go. Is that all?
Thank you! Here is your change.

conversations.title: Making plans
conversations.scene: Friday afternoon. Your friend Rūta sends you a message.

lines.en: Hi! What are you doing at the weekend?

lines.text: Šeštadienį einu į kiną. Ar nori eiti kartu?
lines.en: On Saturday I'm going to the cinema. Do you want to go together?
Seven works! Where shall we meet?
Eight is too late. Maybe seven?
I'm already here. Where are you?

conversations.title: Ar gali padėti?
conversations.scene: Jonas is moving to a new flat this weekend. He calls you.

lines.text: Labas! Ar gali man padėti šeštadienį?
lines.en: Hi! Can you help me on Saturday?
I can't. I have to work.

lines.text: Ar moki vairuoti? Aš turiu mašiną, bet esu pavargęs.
lines.en: Can you drive? I have a car, but I'm tired.
Help me, please! (The sofa is very heavy.)
Thanks! Do you want to eat?
No, thanks. I want to sleep.

lines.text: Ačiū už viską! Ar tau reikia pinigų?
lines.en: Thanks for everything! Do you need money for a taxi?

conversations.title: Ką veiki savaitgalį?
conversations.scene: Friday after work. You and Rūta have a coffee and talk about the weekend.

lines.en: Friday already! What are you up to?

lines.text: Aš? Savaitgalį žaidžiu krepšinį. Ar tau patinka krepšinis?
lines.en: Me? At the weekend I play basketball. Do you like basketball?
Great! In Lithuania everyone plays basketball!
What?! In Lithuania everyone plays basketball!
And what do you like to do?
Great! I like to cook too.

lines.text: O muzika? Ar tau patinka muzika?
lines.en: And music? Do you like music?
OK, I need to go. Bye!

conversations.title: Checking in
conversations.scene: You arrive at your hotel in Klaipėda. Darius is at reception.

lines.en: Good afternoon! I have a reservation.
Thank you. Here is the key.
It's here, on the key card.
Good evening! How can I help?
Sorry! Someone will come right away.

conversations.title: At the pharmacy
conversations.scene: You wake up with a headache and walk into a pharmacy (vaistinė).

lines.en: Good afternoon. How can I help?

lines.text: Štai vaistai. Viena tabletė, tris kartus per dieną.
lines.en: Here is the medicine. One tablet, three times a day.

lines.text: Viena tabletė. Tris kartus per dieną.
lines.en: One tablet. Three times a day.
Got it. How much is it?

conversations.title: Dinner with friends
conversations.scene: Rūta invites you to dinner at her flat. Jonas is there too. Use everything you know.

lines.en: Good evening! This is a gift for you.

lines.text: Gerai, bet šiandien esu labai pavargęs.
lines.en: Good, but I'm very tired today.
Are you hungry? I have cepelinai!

lines.text: Nieko tokio! Turiu ir sriubos. Skanaus!
lines.en: No problem! I have soup too. Enjoy!
Yes, a lot! Vilnius is very beautiful.
And what are you doing tomorrow?
Great! My mom lives in Kaunas.
Thank you very much! See you later!

conversations.title: Kiek kainuoja?
conversations.scene: There is a little kiosk near your home. Birutė, a friendly older woman, runs it, and her grandson often helps.

lines.en: Good afternoon! What can I get you?
Good afternoon! How much is the coffee?
Cake is one euro. How many?

lines.text: Trys pyragai ir kava. Penki eurai.
lines.en: Three cakes and the coffee. Five euros.
Thanks. Here are five euros back.
And you? How old are you? (Lukas wants to know.)
Thank you very much! See you again!

conversations.title: Kada susitinkame?
conversations.scene: Jonas wants to go to the museum with you this week. He texts you while you are at work.

lines.en: Hi! Are you working right now?
Are you working tomorrow? (She wants to go to the museum with you.)
At the Cathedral. (There is a café there.)
OK! Shall we go to the museum?

conversations.title: My day
conversations.scene: Rūta is curious how your days go in Vilnius, from morning to night.

lines.en: Hi! When do you get up?

lines.text: Aš irgi! Ar tu dirbi iš namų?
lines.en: Me too! Do you work from home?

lines.text: Ne. Kartais aš dirbu iš namų.
lines.en: No. Sometimes I work from home.

lines.text: Aš grįžtu namo ir gaminu vakarienę.
lines.en: I come home and cook dinner.

lines.text: Puiku. Aš kasdien žiūriu filmą! O tu?
lines.en: Great. I watch a film every day! And you?
And how much do you sleep?

lines.text: Aštuonias! Gerai. Ar tu kartais vėluoji?
lines.en: Eight! Good. Are you ever late?

conversations.title: Buying a jacket
conversations.scene: It's getting cold, so you go into a clothes shop. Inga works there.

lines.en: Here you go. The fitting room is there.
It doesn't fit. Is there a bigger one?
It fits! How much is it?
That's expensive! Is there a discount?
Today there's a ten percent discount.
OK. But the discount is only today!

conversations.title: Holiday plans
conversations.scene: Summer is coming. Jonas asks about your holiday plans.

lines.en: Hi! Where will you go on holiday?
In summer I'll go to the seaside.
How long will you be there?
I will be there for a week.
No, I will go by bus.
And what will you do tomorrow?

conversations.title: The weekend
conversations.scene: It's Monday. Rūta wants to hear about your weekend.

lines.en: And what did you do there?
Yes, we ate at a restaurant.
I liked it a lot, but it was expensive.

lines.text: Aš buvau namie, nes buvo šalta.
lines.en: I was at home, because it was cold.
What did you do at home?
Nice! Shall we go together next weekend?

conversations.title: Dinner debate
conversations.scene: Dinner with Rūta and Jonas again. This time they want your opinions. Use everything you know.

lines.text: Aš manau, kad Kaunas gražesnis už Vilnių.
lines.en: I think Kaunas is more beautiful than Vilnius.
Really? What do you think, Tomas?
I disagree. Vilnius is very beautiful.
Because I like the old town.
Well, I disagree! Vilnius is more beautiful.

lines.text: Gerai, gerai. O kas geriau, kava ar arbata?
lines.en: OK, OK. And what's better, coffee or tea?

lines.text: Aš manau, kad arbata geresnė už kavą.
lines.en: I think tea is better than coffee.
And what will you do tomorrow?

lines.text: Rytoj aš dirbsiu, bet vakare aš būsiu namie.
lines.en: Tomorrow I'll work, but in the evening I'll be at home.

grammar.name: "To be": am, are, is
grammar.note: Each "who" has its own form. Yra also means "there is".

grammar.name: My and your
grammar.note: These never change: mano vardas, tavo vardas.

grammar.name: How many euros
grammar.note: The number decides the ending of the word after it.

grammar.name: The thing you eat or drink
grammar.note: The "what" of a sentence ends in -ą, -į or -ę.

grammar.name: Some of it
grammar.note: After noriu the thing takes the "some of" ending: kava → kavos, arbata → arbatos.

grammar.name: Describing words match
grammar.note: -as for a "him" word, -a for a "her" word.

grammar.name: Who does it: the ending
grammar.note: -u for I, -i for you. Ne- in front means "not".

grammar.name: Asking a question
rows: Do you speak English? (yes or no)
grammar.note: Ar at the start makes a yes/no question. Question words go first too.

grammar.name: From, and in
grammar.note: "From" is iš plus a new ending. "In" is only an ending.

grammar.name: I will
grammar.note: Add -s- before the ending: dirbu → dirbsiu.

grammar.name: I did
grammar.note: -au for I, -o for he and she.

canDo: say I don't understand and ask for help
introduce myself and say where I'm from
ask how someone is, and answer
ask the way and follow directions
take a bus, train or taxi
offer help, or say I can't
give reasons with because, but and though
find my way in a new town

path.sub: Sounds, greetings and help when you get stuck
Who you are, where you are, actions and questions
Count, tell the time and describe a routine
Say what you eat and order a meal
Find places, travel, shop and choose clothes
Family, home, descriptions, feelings and work
Interests, what you can do, invitations and dates
Connect ideas, talk about yesterday and give background
Hotels, journeys and explaining a problem
Share opinions, keep talking and stay in touch
Animals, food, culture and one final conversation

units.title: Sonidos
units.tip: Spanish spelling gives you reliable clues to pronunciation. Its five vowels sound like ah, eh, ee, oh and oo: keep them short and clear. A few letters trick English speakers: j is a breathy "h", ll sounds like the start of "yes" in Mexican Spanish, ñ sounds like the middle of "canyon", and h is silent. These words have familiar English relatives to help you get started.

units.title: Lo básico
units.tip: Start with Hola: it works with anyone, at any time of day. You can also choose a greeting for the time of day: Buenos días in the morning, Buenas tardes in the afternoon, and Buenas noches after dark.

items.en: I am from the United States

units.title: Plática
units.tip: Most chats start the same way. Someone asks ¿Cómo estás?, you answer with Bien, gracias or Más o menos, and you bounce it back with ¿Y tú?

items.en: How do you say it in Spanish?

units.title: Ser y estar
units.tip: Use soy for your identity and eres when asking a friend about theirs. A job normally needs no word for “a”.

items.en: he / she / it is (state or location)
they / you all are (state or location)

units.title: Lo que hacemos
units.tip: For these regular verbs, the “I” form ends in -o and the informal “you” form ends in -as.

units.title: Preguntas
units.tip: Question words carry written accents. Choose the one that asks for the kind of information you need.

units.title: Sobre mí
units.tip: Use de for origin. Keep the name of your country after it.

units.title: Números
units.tip: Say the numbers in order, then mix them up. Practise hearing each number on its own.

units.title: El tiempo
units.tip: Days of the week are normally written with lowercase letters in Spanish.

units.title: Mi día
units.tip: In these actions, me shows that you do something involving yourself. Keep it before the conjugated verb.

items.en: Do you eat breakfast at eight?
What time do you go to bed?

units.title: Comida y bebida
units.tip: Learn the article with each food. The noun keeps its form when it is the thing you eat.

units.title: En el restaurante
units.tip: Polite requests can be short. Add por favor after what you need.

units.title: La ciudad
units.tip: Use el or la with each place. These nouns will help you ask where things are.

units.title: Direcciones
units.tip: Use these short phrases to follow directions. Practise pointing as you say them.

items.en: It is next to the bank

units.title: Transporte
units.tip: These are common transport words in Mexico. Learn the noun and its article together.

items.en: I want to go to the airport

units.title: De compras
units.tip: These words help you identify an item and ask its price.

items.en: I do not need a bag

units.title: Ropa
units.tip: Clothing words have a grammatical gender even when anyone can wear the item.

items.en: Can I try it on? (the jacket)
Do you want a smaller size?
Would you like it in blue? (polite)
It is too small on me (feminine item)

units.title: Familia
units.tip: The article is part of the noun phrase. Keep the masculine and feminine family terms distinct.

units.title: La casa
units.tip: Learn each noun with its article, then picture where it is in your home.

units.title: Describir
units.tip: Many describing words end in -o for a masculine noun and -a for a feminine noun.

units.title: Cómo me siento
units.tip: Use the state verb for how you feel now. Some of these words have a different form for women.

units.title: Trabajo
units.tip: A profession normally follows the identity verb without an article. Some job words change for women.

items.en: What do you do for work?
I do not work on Sundays

units.title: Tiempo libre
units.tip: Dictionary forms end in -ar, -er or -ir. Learn the whole form for an activity.

units.title: Poder y necesitar
units.tip: Keep the second verb in its dictionary form after the word for “can”.

items.en: I do not want to go out

units.title: Planes
units.tip: For a plan, put a between the form of “go” and the dictionary form of the activity.

items.en: What are you going to do tomorrow?
Shall we go to the cinema?
Do you want to eat with me?
I cannot; I have to work

items.text: Está bien, nos vemos a las seis

units.title: El año
units.tip: Use these season names to talk about weather or travel plans.

units.title: Unir ideas
units.tip: These short words connect two ideas. Keep the relationship between those ideas clear.

items.en: I want to go but I cannot
I am not going because I am tired

units.title: Ayer
units.tip: These time expressions often go with completed past actions. Learn the irregular past forms as whole words.

items.en: I was (state or location, completed period)
Yesterday I went to the market

units.title: Contar historias
units.tip: Use these expressions to organise the order of events. They can introduce a short past-tense sentence.

items.en: I / he / she used to be (identity)
I / he / she was (state or location)
I / he / she had / used to have
I / he / she used to live
I / he / she used to go / was going
I used to live in Mexico
I used to have a dog

items.text: Iba al parque todos los días
items.en: I used to go to the park every day
How did it go for you?
First I ate, then I went out
In the end I returned home
Where did you live when you were a child?
Did you go to the market?

units.title: En el hotel
units.tip: Use a polite request at reception. Say the noun clearly, then add the details.

items.en: It is on the second floor

units.title: De viaje
units.tip: Keep the article with each travel noun. These are useful words at an airport or hotel.

items.en: I want a ticket to Mexico
How long does the trip take?

units.title: Salud y ayuda
units.tip: Learn body nouns with their articles. They help you describe a problem clearly.

items.en: Do you have something for a cough?
I am allergic to this medicine
I need to speak with a doctor

units.title: Opiniones
units.tip: Use these short openings to express a view. You can add a complete sentence after them.

items.text: No me gustan los hoteles grandes
items.en: I do not like big hotels
I think it is very expensive
Does that sound good to you?

units.title: Seguir la plática
units.tip: A short reaction shows that you are following the conversation. Match your tone to the meaning.

items.en: It was lovely to see you
Have a good day (to a friend)

units.title: Mensajes
units.tip: Use these nouns when exchanging contact details or asking for internet access.

items.en: I will send you a message
Can you write it for me? (polite)
Could you bring me water, please?
Can you call me a taxi?
I need to charge my phone
Where can I buy a ticket?

units.title: Animales
units.tip: Learn each animal with its article. Some animal nouns have different male and female forms.

units.title: México
units.tip: These food names are useful in Mexico. Some do not have a single-word English equivalent.

items.en: right now / in a little while (context matters)
I want to get to know Mexico

conversations.title: ¡Hola, Mariana!
conversations.scene: You are Tomás, on your first morning in Mexico City. The café in Coyoacán is busy, and the only free seat is next to a woman with a coffee.

lines.en: Very well, thanks. How are you?
I am from the United States.

lines.text: Ay, me tengo que ir. Voy al museo.
lines.en: Oh, I have to go. I'm going to the museum.

conversations.title: Otra vez, por favor
conversations.scene: The next day you meet Mariana again, on a bench in Parque México. She talks fast. That's fine: you know how to slow her down.

lines.en: How cool! Do you speak Spanish?

lines.text: ¡Hoy hace un día padrísimo! ¿Vamos a caminar por el parque y luego nos tomamos un café?
lines.en: It's a gorgeous day today! Shall we walk through the park and then have a coffee?
Shall we... go for a walk?
To walk... like this! (She walks two fingers along the bench.)
How do you say it in Spanish?

lines.text: Bueno, ya me voy. ¡Que tengas un buen día!
lines.en: Well, I'm off now. Have a good day!

conversations.title: ¿Dónde vives?
conversations.scene: Mariana meets you at the café again. This time you can say more about yourself.

lines.en: Very well. Where are you from?
I am from the United States.

conversations.title: Mi mañana
conversations.scene: Diego asks about your daily routine over an afternoon coffee.

lines.en: Very well. What time is it?

conversations.title: Una mesa para dos
conversations.scene: Mariana is helping out at a small restaurant. Practise ordering and paying.

lines.text: Una mesa para dos, por favor.

lines.en: I do not eat meat. I want soup.

lines.text: Un café con leche, por favor.

conversations.title: Al museo
conversations.scene: You ask Diego how to get to the museum, then check which way to go.

lines.en: Excuse me. Can you help me?
It is nearby. Go straight ahead.

lines.text: Dos cuadras. Gire a la derecha.

lines.en: Are you going to the park?
I am going to the park.
No. I am going to the museum.

conversations.title: Un boleto
conversations.scene: Mariana helps you work out the journey to the airport.

lines.en: Do you want to go to the airport?
Yes. I want to go to the airport.
No. I am going by bus.

conversations.title: Una chamarra azul
conversations.scene: You are choosing a jacket in a shop. Ask about size and price.

lines.en: Yes. How much does it cost?
Do you want a smaller size?
I do not need a bag.

conversations.title: Mi familia
conversations.scene: Diego tells you about his family and asks about yours.

lines.en: What do you do for work?

conversations.title: Planes para mañana
conversations.scene: Mariana invites you out tomorrow. Agree on an activity and a time.

lines.en: What are you going to do tomorrow?
Do you want to eat with me?
I cannot; I have to work.
OK. Shall we go to the cinema?

lines.text: Voy a viajar la próxima semana.
lines.en: I am going to travel next week.

conversations.title: ¿Qué hiciste ayer?
conversations.scene: After the weekend, Mariana asks you what happened. Practise a short story.

lines.en: Yesterday I went to the market.
In the end I returned home.
Where did you live when you were a child?
I used to live in Mexico.
I used to have a dog.

conversations.title: En la recepción
conversations.scene: You arrive at a hotel and check the room details.

lines.en: It is on the second floor.

conversations.title: Necesito ayuda
conversations.scene: You feel ill and ask Mariana to help you find a doctor.

lines.en: Yes. We are going by taxi.
I need to speak with a doctor.
I am allergic to this medicine.

conversations.title: Una buena plática
conversations.scene: At dinner with Mariana, share preferences, react and make another plan.

lines.en: What do you prefer? Coffee or tea?
What are you going to do tomorrow?

lines.text: Voy a viajar con mi familia.
lines.en: I am going to travel with my family.
I want to get to know Mexico.
It was lovely to see you.

conversations.title: Nos escribimos
conversations.scene: Exchange contact details and get help with a small problem.

lines.en: Can you write it for me?
I will send you a message.
I need to charge my phone.
Thank you. Let’s keep in touch.

grammar.name: Two ways to be
rows: I am: identity / state or location
you are: identity / state or location
he, she, it or polite you is
grammar.note: Choose the verb by meaning, then choose its form for the subject. Events use ser for their location; do not treat every location as an estar rule.

grammar.name: Regular present endings
grammar.note: The subject word can often be omitted because the ending identifies it.

grammar.name: The time
grammar.note: Use singular at one o’clock and plural for the other hours.

grammar.name: Descriptions agree
grammar.note: Match grammatical gender and number. Not every describing word has a different feminine ending.

grammar.name: Existence and location
grammar.note: Hay introduces existence; estar locates a particular thing.

grammar.name: Saying what you like
grammar.note: The verb agrees with the thing liked: singular for an activity or one thing, plural for more than one.

grammar.name: Two verbs together
grammar.note: The second verb stays in the dictionary form. The obligation expression needs its linking word.

grammar.name: Going to do something
grammar.note: Use a form of ir, then a, then the dictionary form of the activity.

grammar.name: Completed past actions
rows: I went or was / did / had
Yesterday I went to the market
grammar.note: Learn irregular forms as whole words. A written accent on regular past endings affects the stress.

grammar.name: Past events and background
rows: I used to live in Mexico
First I ate, then I went out
grammar.note: The imperfect describes background or habits; the preterite presents completed events. Context determines the choice.

grammar.name: What hurts
grammar.note: The pain verb agrees with the painful body part, rather than with the person experiencing it.

ask how someone is, and answer
say I don't understand and ask for help
